text:
nina-support: heads up — we're getting multiple reports of Dedicated placement failures when failing over from us-east-1 to us-west-2 for Reserved accounts. customer reported 502s + placement errors, and one billing auth 403 spike.

ellis-support: attaching the customer's API call they used
ellis-support: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/dedicated/v1/alloc \n -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX" \n -d '{"region":"us-west-2","size":"large","model":"redwood-7b"}'
```:
ellis-support: response: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"placement failed: no GPU capacity available","code":"PLACEMENT_NO_CAPACITY"}

raj-eng-sre: checking infra — I see placement error spikes around 14:07 UTC, and autoscaler logs show repeated create VM attempts throttled by cloud api (429). sample from autoscaler:
raj-eng-sre: ```
ERROR CreateInstance failed: quotaExceeded
status_code=429 details="RateLimitExceeded: Too many create requests"
``` 

toni-runtime: that 429 explains why new nodes didn't come up. autoscaler is limited to 2 concurrent create ops per region (we recently set to conservative values). noisy neighbor churn also triggered intense evictions in us-west-2 yesterday; combined effect = no spare slots.

leo-eng: also saw a couple of auth handshakes failing from the billing service at ~14:09 UTC — looks like an oauth token refresh race produced transient 403 for a handful of customers. link to logs: https://internal/logs/incident/1860123456

maya-csm: customer reported that they were charged for retries — billing team, can we confirm whether failed allocations incur charge? @carter-oncall

carter-oncall: billing confirmed failed placement attempts should not bill for GPU runtime, but allocation attempt fees (api call) may show as minor usage. we'll open an invoice review if customer gets unexpected charges.

nina-support: repro steps for eng to reproduce (used on customer account):
nina-support: 1) POST the allocation request (see curl above) 2) simultaneously send 10 quick retries from client within 10s window 3) observe 503 + PLACEMENT_NO_CAPACITY

raj-eng-sre: mitigation options:
- increase autoscaler parallel creates for us-west-2 to 5 temporarily
- enable cross-region fallback policy to route to eu-west-1 for this customer's Dedicated pool
- add short-term capacity by spinning up warm instances in us-west-2 (manual)

ellis-support: I can route the customer to eu-west-1 standby for now, but they want low-latency — need ETA for us-west-2 fix.

toni-runtime: I'm going to bump parallel creates and start a small warm pool. will monitor. if we see more 429s from cloud provider, we throttle our clients' retry behavior instead and surface 429 to them.

deploy-bot: deploy started by toni-runtime at 2026-03-17T14:22:00Z — autoscaler config patch: parallel_creates: 5

carter-oncall: owner: toni-runtime for immediate mitigation, raj-eng-sre will follow up with postmortem. maya-csm to own customer comms.

nina-support: action items:
- toni-runtime: adjust autoscaler + start warm pool (in progress)
- raj-eng-sre: collect full placement traces and cloud create quotas (ETA 2h)
- billing: review charges for affected accounts (ETA 4h)
- maya-csm: notify customer with fallback option and offer credits

maya-csm: noted, I'll send a short status update to the customer: "we've routed you to eu-west-1 for now; engineering is scaling us-west-2; we'll follow up with root cause and compensation" :thumbsup: 

nina-support: ping if anything changes. I'll keep the thread updated. :eyes:
